subject: Exec briefing: SLA risk, incident synthesis, and QBR OKR impacts
messages:
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 08:15:00 -0800
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Verma <p.verma@acmehealth.com>
Subject: Initial incident synthesis — partial routing failure affecting Acme Health

Tessa / Marcus / Priya,

Quick summary from the SRE shift: on 2026-01-11 22:03 UTC we observed a routing regression in the east-west mesh that caused 503s for a subset of Acme Health traffic for ~42 minutes. Impacted endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings for sessions routed to the dedicated pool. We saw automatic fallback kick in after ~6 minutes but requests queued then experienced elevated latency and a small increase in token cost due to retries.

Key numbers (preliminary):
- Duration: 42 minutes total; major impact window ~22:03–22:45 UTC
- Error rate peak: 28% on affected hosts
- SLO impact (per Acme contract): expected availability drop ~0.75% for the window; still within monthly threshold but a risk for QBR narrative
- Customers explicitly impacted: Acme Health (internal report attached)

Immediate remediation performed: drain + redeploy of 4 hosts, forced route fallback after 6 minutes, incremental scaling to absorb bursts. Root cause (investigation ongoing): an aggressive routing table cleanup combined with an edge config rollback.

Attachments: incident-timeline.csv (raw event times)

Next steps we recommend for exec briefing / QBR prep:
- Produce a one-page SLO impact brief and include action owners (I can draft)
- Decide if we proactively offer a one-time credit to Acme; ops recommends a partial credit tied to retry costs
- Confirm whether this needs an urgent customer call (Priya, do you want a sync?)

I'll follow up with a draft exec slide and clearer RCA by Thursday.

--
Chloe Martin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:03:00 -0800
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Verma <p.verma@acmehealth.com>
Subject: Re: Initial incident synthesis — partial routing failure affecting Acme Health

Thanks Chloe — this is the right level to start with. A few asks before I include in Friday's QBR packet: 

1) Hannah / Marcus: please convert Chloe's bullets into a 1-slide exec summary (SLO delta, customer impact, top 3 mitigations and ETA). Slide should open with the customer-facing delta and end with owner+ETA for each action.
2) Chloe: add estimated token cost delta for the retry window (ballpark is fine).
3) Leadership decision: Vivek, do you want the credit discussed now or wait for full RCA? If we do offer something, I want a proposed template (amount, conditions, PR language).
4) Priya — if you want a customer call, propose 2x 30-min slots tomorrow; otherwise we'll prepare the customer note.

I'll fold the slide into the QBR packet draft and circulate to execs by EOD Thursday; if we need to push a customer-facing communication earlier we can.

Thanks,
Tessa
Head of Customer Success (Interim)
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 10:18:00 -0800
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>, Priya Verma <p.verma@acmehealth.com>
Subject: Re: Exec briefing: SLA risk, incident synthesis, and QBR OKR impacts

Appreciate the quick triage. A few points from leadership: 

- Prioritize a crisp SLO impact matrix (customer-level and aggregate). This is what execs will want to see in the QBR.
- I prefer we prepare a customer credit proposal now (not awaiting full RCA). Use a conservative template: credit equals estimated incremental retry cost + goodwill up to $X (we'll discuss exact cap offline). Programmatically flag accounts where monthly SLO drift >0.5%.
- For OKR implications: list which reliability OKRs are at risk this quarter (e.g., "Reduce transient SLO breaches" or "Improve routing failover median <1s"). Mark owners so product/RTEs can re-prioritize.

Hannah — can you take lead on the SLO matrix and action rollup? Tessa, partner with Marcus on customer comms and credit wording. Chloe, keep the RCA thread live and attach a timeline artifact.

Vivek
CEO, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 08:50:00 -0800
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>, Priya Verma <p.verma@acmehealth.com>
Subject: Re: Exec briefing: SLA risk, incident synthesis, and QBR OKR impacts — action rollup v1

Team — attaching the first-pass action rollup and SLO impact summary (attached as action-rollup.xlsx and slo-impact-summary.pdf). Highlights: 

1) SLO matrix (by customer + aggregate): Acme recorded a 0.72% availability drop for Jan 11 window; cohort impact for dedicated-pool customers shows mean delta 0.3% for the day.
2) Proposed credits: incrementals only — estimated retry token overcharge for Acme: ~$1,250. Recommend offering a $2,000 credit (covers cost + goodwill).
3) Action owners + ETA: 
   - Root cause RCA (Chloe) — draft by 2026-01-15 EOD
   - Routing fallback hardening (SRE infra) — Marcus to propose kernel change by 2026-01-22
   - Playbook update (failover timing and automatic forced fallback) — Hannah to deliver updated doc and runbook by 2026-01-19
   - Customer comms and credit note (Tessa + Marcus) — draft customer note by 2026-01-14 5pm PT

Questions for leadership: do we want to log this as a "QBR highlight" (transparency + corrective actions) or bury it in the operational appendix? My recommendation: highlight it as an example of improved detection/fallback and tie it to the OKR remediation plan.

--
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Reliability Engineering
